source_finding.layer: Complete Wellmann critical-edition II.164 sections1-4 from cached XML and paired JSON, not a complete diplomatic Morgan M.652 transcription.
section3_sequence: The root is cut and squeezed: the root is the material subjected to extraction.
Its juice is boiled to honey-like consistency: juice bears this physical thickening operation and endpoint.
The next clause explicitly re-names root as grammatical subject of skin-cleansing, rash-reduction and wound-healing assertions.
Subsequent external-use clauses continue the root, followed by separately named decoction and an old-oil boiling/application construction.
source_finding.nontrivial_local_consequence: A source-faithful II.164 account cannot use nearest-mentioned juice as the automatic subject of the explicit root-effect clause. A physical honey-consistency endpoint does not establish a clinical effect, execution completion, or effect transfer to an extracted product.
source_finding.important_counterexample: Section2 explicitly assigns other applications/effects to juice. Therefore the section3 root subject does not imply that juice has no effects, or that root and juice effects can never overlap. Source-owned grammatical assignment is narrower than an exclusive clinical claim.
source_finding.complete_context: Section4 hollowing/filling the root with oil, hot-ash warming, optional wax, storage, burning/pastilles and habitat are preserved; no extraction-only quotation is presented as a whole entry.

novelty_decision.falsifier: For a separately declared whole-context II.164 C0 reading, reject source-content adequacy if extraction/thickening is assigned to root instead of juice, if the following explicit root effects are automatically assigned to juice without a paid written source/target relation, or if a clinical effect is inferred solely from honey-consistency. novelty_decision.review_ceiling: Retain RAW825 as a sensible source-grounded C0 constraint. Do not select it as an independent meaning anchor or reopen closed tests. Lack of 100-percent semantic proof does not forbid coherent hypothesis authorship.

If both fixed candidates give the same unbound bearer placeholders, or adequate reading requires silently changing a word/host/phase, no further ownership test is justified.
